subsystems.name: Antenna and receiver
subsystems.role: collects faint radio emission from selected stars or sky regions.
parts: large dish antennas (e.g. Green Bank Telescope, FAST, Parkes)

subsystems.name: Digital backend
subsystems.role: turns analogue voltages into high-resolution frequency channels and time samples.
parts: FPGA or GPU-based polyphase filter banks

subsystems.name: Signal search pipeline
subsystems.role: searches for narrowband carriers that drift in frequency due to Doppler shifts.

subsystems.name: Interference mitigation
subsystems.role: rejects signals from terrestrial transmitters, satellites and electronic equipment.

subsystems.name: Verification system
subsystems.role: confirms candidate signals by re-observing them with an independent telescope.
parts: access to a second telescope at a different site

subsystems.name: Data management
subsystems.role: stores raw and processed data for analysis and later re-examination.

buildSteps.title: Select targets
buildSteps.detail: Choose nearby stars, known exoplanet systems, the Galactic plane and other regions where a transmitter might be expected.

buildSteps.title: Observe with a radio telescope
buildSteps.detail: Point the dish and record raw voltages or channelised data, often while nodding on and off the target to separate local interference.

buildSteps.title: Digitise and channelise
buildSteps.detail: Convert the analogue signal into thousands or millions of narrow frequency channels, each sampled many times per second.

buildSteps.title: Search for drifting narrowband signals
buildSteps.detail: Apply algorithms that look for narrow peaks shifting in frequency over time, as a transmitter on a moving planet would appear.

buildSteps.title: Filter interference
buildSteps.detail: Compare with RFI databases, monitor reference antennas and reject signals that appear in all directions or match known transmitters.

buildSteps.title: Identify candidates
buildSteps.detail: Cluster and rank surviving signals by strength, drift rate and persistence, producing a short list for follow-up.

buildSteps.title: Re-observe with an independent telescope
buildSteps.detail: Point a different dish at the same target at the same time; a real extraterrestrial signal should appear in both, while interference usually does not.

buildSteps.title: Follow up and analyse
buildSteps.detail: If confirmed, study the signal for repetition, modulation, polarisation and any other properties that distinguish technology from nature.

buildSteps.title: Archive the data
buildSteps.detail: Store raw and processed data so that future, more powerful search algorithms can re-examine past observations.

prerequisites.tech: Large single-dish and array radio telescopes
prerequisites.why: sensitivity is limited by collecting area, so big dishes are essential to detect weak or distant transmitters.
covering many frequencies at once increases the chance of catching a signal at an unknown frequency.
surveys generate terabytes per hour and require real-time or near-real-time processing.
terrestrial interference is the dominant source of false positives and is increasingly hard to avoid.
narrowband drifting carrier searches are well developed, but they only cover one class of possible transmission.
a candidate must be confirmed by a second instrument to rule out local interference.

pathway.milestone: ongoing surveys such as those by the SETI Institute and Breakthrough Listen on telescopes like the Green Bank Telescope, Parkes and FAST
pathway.unlocks: coverage of thousands of nearby stars and wide swathes of the Galactic plane.

pathway.milestone: next-generation facilities such as the Square Kilometre Array and the next-generation Very Large Array begin operations
pathway.unlocks: orders of magnitude more sensitivity and survey speed, reaching much fainter or more distant signals.

pathway.milestone: commensal and real-time surveys that piggyback on other observations
pathway.unlocks: continuous sky monitoring with rapid follow-up of any candidate.

pathway.milestone: coordinated radio, optical and infrared technosignature searches
pathway.unlocks: more robust confirmation and characterisation if a signal is found.

pathway.milestone: a detected and independently verified signal triggers international protocols for confirmation and announcement
pathway.unlocks: a scientific and societal response to the first evidence of an extraterrestrial technology.
